**Description**
 We are responsible for billions of dollars of payments each month to millions of Amazon vendors across the globe. We delight our vendors by paying them when they want and how they want, accurately and on time.
   

  

 We build software applications that facilitate global financial transactions worth billions (USD) annually, rivaling the complexity and scope of dedicated payments fintech companies. Our systems decide how and when a payment happens, carry it out across the world's payment networks, and account for it — all under real regulatory, tax, and audit obligations, in every geography Amazon operates in.
   

  

 You will have the opportunity to work in a high\-paced environment leveraging the AI\-Driven Development Lifecycle (AIDLC) within our core principles of engineering, to deliver faster and ship features incrementally.
   

  

 Ownership is the center of this role, and ownership here means the whole lifecycle rather than just the code. You will take features from working backwards from the customer through design, implementation, testing, deployment, and documentation — and you stay accountable for how they behave in production long after they ship.
   

  

 Own features and components of our payment systems end\-to\-end. The business problem and the technology direction will be understood; how to actually build it will not be, and that part is yours.
   

  

 Design the solution and make the tradeoffs. You will code independently, and you will have senior and principal engineers to pull in when a tradeoff is genuinely hard or when a design needs to line up with where the architecture is heading.
   

  

 Work directly with product managers and business stakeholders — finance, tax, and accounts payable operations — to understand what they need and why, so that you build the right thing. You will hear the requirement first\-hand rather than through a written hand\-off, and you will be expected to push back when the ask and the outcome do not line up.
   

  

 Ship incrementally. Large payment changes land safely through staged rollout and measurement, not through a single release.
   

  

 Reduce operational load. Our best work turns a recurring manual intervention into a code fix or a self\-healing mechanism, not another runbook step.
   

  

 Leave the system better explained than you found it. What you build should be maintainable and extensible by an engineer who has never seen it, which means clear documentation and design choices that hold up without you in the room.
   

  

 Raise the bar around you: code review as a teaching mechanism, mentoring engineers earlier in their careers, and getting new teammates productive on how our software is built, how it operates, and how it fits into the bigger picture.
   

  

 Building with agentic AI
   

  

 We are not experimenting with AI on the side — it is how we work. You will use AI agents across the development lifecycle: exploring unfamiliar systems, drafting and reviewing designs, generating and testing code, triaging production issues, and automating the operational work that used to consume a week of on\-call. We expect engineers to be strong directors of these agents and rigorous verifiers of their output. The judgment stays with you: you are accountable for what ships, whether you typed it or an agent did. Agentic capabilities are increasingly part of the systems themselves — automating decisions and investigations that previously required a human in the loop — and you will have room to build them.
   

  

 Why this team
   

  

 Payments is one of the few places in software where the business logic is genuinely hard, the scale is enormous, and a mistake has an immediate real\-world consequence — a vendor who does not get paid when they expected. If you want real ownership, global scope, and the freedom to build with the newest tools available rather than waiting for permission to try them, this is a good place to build a career.

* 3\+ years of non\-internship professional software development experience
* 2\+ years of non\-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
* 1\+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
* 1\+ years of designing and developing large\-scale, multi\-tiered, multi\-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C\#, C\+\+, Java, or Perl experience
* 1\+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
* Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
* Experience programming with at least one software programming language


**Preferred Qualifications**
* 3\+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
* Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
* Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems
* Experience debugging, profiling, and implementing best software engineering practices in large\-scale systems

* Hands\-on experience using AI coding agents in real production work, with a clear point of view on where they help and where their output needs to be checked.

You will be required to understand how these models work inside-out to make informed decisions on how to best coax the compiler to generate optimal implementation instruction. You will leverage your technical communications skill to partner with internal and external customers/stakeholders and will be involved in pre-silicon design, bringing new products/features to market, ultimately, making Neuron compiler highly performant and easy-to-use.
  
  
Experience in object-oriented languages like C++/Java is a must, experience with compilers or building ML models using ML frameworks on accelerators (e.g., GPUs) is preferred but not required.
  
  
Experience with technologies like OpenXLA, StableHLO, MLIR will be added bonus!

**Overview**
Intuit Enterprise Suite is how the world's fastest-growing mid-market and enterprise finance teams run their books, close their quarter, and put AI agents to work on real accounting operations — not demos. Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) are the team that makes that real: embedded with our customers, shipping production automation, and turning “AI pilot” into “AI in the general ledger.”
  
  
This isn't a traditional sales engineering role, and it isn't a traditional product engineering role either. FDEs report into Engineering, work shoulder-to-shoulder with Sales and Account Management on the deals and renewals that matter most, and own the last mile between what Core Engineering ships and what a specific customer actually runs. You'll sit at the intersection of engineering, applied AI, and enterprise finance, and you'll be judged on one thing: did the customer's business measurably change because you were in the room.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**What you'll do**
Pre-sale: build the proof that wins the deal
  
  

* Get hands-on with prospects before there's a contract: build a working proof-of-value directly in (or against a realistic replica of) the prospect's own data and systems — real integrations and real output, not a scripted demo.
* Partner with Account Executives from first technical touch: run discovery with the prospect's finance and IT teams to understand their chart of accounts, systems, and process gaps well enough to build against them.
* Lead the technical evaluation: architecture and security/compliance reviews, integration feasibility, and technical RFP responses with the prospect's IT and controllership teams.
* Build the technical narrative and ROI case alongside Sales, and present it directly to economic buyers — CFOs and Controllers — as part of the deal cycle. Your proof-of-value is very often what gets the deal signed.
* Flag technical or data-readiness risk early, so Sales scopes and prices the deal accurately and nothing you built pre-sale becomes a surprise post-signature.

Post-sale: architect and ship in customer specific production
  
  

* Architect and deploy customer-specific configurations of AI Agents that automate complex accounting processes — strengthening internal controls, closing books faster, and removing manual work from real customer environments.
* Perform deep technical troubleshooting: review and edit Python, write SQL for integrations, and diagnose configuration issues across customer systems.
* Serve as the functional and technical escalation point for issues involving integrations, data flows, and automation logic — including reviewing and optimizing SQL-based validations and API-driven workflows.
* Maintain SLAs for response and resolution; document issues comprehensively and escalate to Engineering with complete context.

Post-sale: own the customer relationship and drive expansion
  
  

* Lead high-impact transformation engagements with enterprise finance teams — diagnosing operational bottlenecks and identifying where AI Agents create the most leverage.
* Act as the primary technical point of contact across implementations, engaging directly with CFOs, Controllers, and accounting leaders.
* Guide and train customer teams through workflow redesign, change management, and the value realization required to scale AI Agent adoption across their organization — and carry that same proof-of-value discipline into expansion and renewal conversations.
* Travel to customer sites as needed (up to 70%) for pre-sale technical evaluation, hands-on deployment, training, and adoption workshops.

Ongoing: shape the product and the playbook
  
  

* Be the Voice of the Customer: surface technical feedback, integration requirements, and product gaps to Product and Core Engineering — as input to their roadmap, not a substitute for it.
* Partner with Product Management on learnings from onsite discovery sessions to design workflows centered on AI Agent deployment and business outcomes.
* Build the playbook: create implementation guides, expansion frameworks, and reusable assets so every deployment makes the next one faster.
* Educate customers and internal teams on the strategic value of AI-enabled workflow transformation and best practices for building durable AI Agents.

**Where this role sits**
FDEs report into Engineering, not Sales — but this is very much a field role, spanning both sides of the signature, and the two partnerships below are the job as much as the code is.
  
  
Your partnership with Sales & Account Management
  
  

* You're the technical face of Enterprise Suite in the field, on both sides of the deal: Account Executives pull you in pre-sale to build the proof-of-value that wins the technical evaluation, and Customer Success pulls you in post-sale for QBRs, renewals, and expansion.
* Deals and renewals in this business run on proof, not promises — you're the one who produces it, first as a working pilot in the sales cycle, then as a live production system afterward. That makes you directly responsible for de-risking the pipeline, even though you don't carry a number yourself.
* You'll work daily with Account Executives and Customer Success on the accounts you're assigned to; you won't be measured on bookings, but expect to be in the room for the technical parts of both the sale and the renewal.

Your partnership with Core Engineering
  
  

* You build on top of what Core Engineering ships — you're not a parallel path to the platform roadmap, and this role doesn't re-architect the core product.
* Your job is the last-mile layer: wiring existing AI Agent capabilities into one customer's specific data, workflows, and edge cases, fast enough to prove value inside a live deal.
* In return, you feed Core Engineering structured signal — the patterns that show up across multiple customers — so they can decide what to productize. FDE work should make the core roadmap sharper, never duplicate it or bypass it.

**Qualifications**
What you'll bring
  
  
**Required**

* 3-5 years in Forward Deployed Engineering, Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, technical consulting, or a comparable hands-on, customer-embedded engineering role (scope and level matched to experience — see Levels & Compensation below).
* Deep experience with Agentic AI: LangChain, LangGraph, MCP servers, multi-agent, RAG, vector stores, hybrid retrieval
* Experience with LLMs & tooling: OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic; GitHub Copilot, Gemini Code Assist; prompt engineering
* Deep experience with REST APIs, GraphQL, webhooks, SQL, and enterprise integrations.
* Strong technical fluency and the ability to collaborate deeply with Product Managers and Engineers as a peer, not a hand-off.
* A track record of managing multiple technical deployments simultaneously under delivery pressure.
* Comfort leading technical troubleshooting calls with customers and internal IT teams.
* Comfortable operating on both sides of the signature — building a credible proof-of-value under sales-cycle time pressure, and running that same system reliably in production afterward.
* You default to automation — you use AI and modern tooling to move faster, document better, and scale your own impact.
* Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguity into executable requirements, and to communicate insights clearly to both engineers and executives.
* Strong commercial awareness, stakeholder management, and the ability to operate effectively under delivery and revenue pressure.

**Preferred**

* Background in high-growth SaaS, applied AI, or fintech/ERP/accounting-adjacent domains.
* Domain experience in one of our priority verticals — construction (job costing, WIP, retainage), nonprofit (fund accounting, grant and donor compliance), manufacturing (inventory, cost accounting, production workflows), wealth management (client billing, compliance/regulatory reporting, investment accounting), health care (revenue cycle, compliance-heavy financial operations), franchise (zee governance, zor performance), or field services (job/work-order costing, scheduling-linked billing). You don't need more than one, but depth in any single vertical materially shortens ramp-up on real customer engagements.
* Non-traditional paths are a plus: veterans, former management consultants, competitive programmers, and PhDs have historically made excellent FDEs.
* Prior experience embedded at a customer site for a multi-month deployment (implementation consulting, forward-deployed, or field engineering background).
